accepted.evidence: Andersen prints ciraṭhitika 'perpetual, lasting long' beside Sanskrit cirasthitika and Pali ciratthitika, explicitly cross-referring to cira and thitika. Turner 4824 documents cira in Ashokan compounds and 13770 explicitly lists Ashokan cira/cila-thitika forms. Preserve both ordered lexical components.
Andersen's printed caka line says 'see saka'. The source's adjective saka 'able, possible' is linked to Turner 12253; the separate Buddhist noun saka has a different ID and is excluded.
Andersen's printed chavachara line says 'see saṃvachara'. The year head is the linked source samvacʰara, from Turner 13011 saṁvatsará; preserve the documented Rupnath spelling as a source variant.
Andersen's printed sāvāna line says 'see sāvana' for the Sahasram spelling. The source head sāvana 'announcement, edict' is already linked to Turner 12698 śrāvaṇa 'announcing'.

Andersen prints jānapada 'belonging to the country' beside ŚB jānapada and Pali janapada, cross-referring to the source's janapada 'country'. Turner 5101 explicitly distinguishes Ashokan Kalsi janapade from Girnar jānapadasa 'living in the country' < jānapadá. Record the adjective's transparent derivation from the already-linked same-source noun rather than collapse the nominal and adjectival formations.
